questiontext.text:
Goal

A lost property counter accepts any item that a passenger hands over, including nothing. The clerk gives every item a name and keeps the counter open when an unfamiliar item arrives. The clerk names nothing at all empty hands. The clerk names any item he does not recognise, including a number with a decimal part, unclaimed. When the clerk counts coins and the item is not coins, the count is 0, the answer is false, and the counter stays open.

Read
  • Type switches. Read the two paragraphs after the grammar block. What can a case use instead of a type? When does that case match?
  • Type assertions. Which assertion form stops the run when the stored value has a different type? What does the other form return?
  • Interface types. Find the empty interface. Which predeclared one-word name can replace it?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a null check followed by a chain of instanceof tests. One Go statement does both jobs, and Go has no catch clause for a conversion that fails.

if (item == null) return "empty hands";
if (item instanceof Integer n) return n + " coins";
Banned: if, ==, !=
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If describe prints unclaimed for nothing at all, reread the Type switches paragraph that mentions a predeclared identifier.
  • If a test ends the run instead of printing, count the names on the left of your assertion. Then reread the last paragraph of Type assertions.

expected.text: a note reading meet me at platform 2

questiontext.text:
Goal

A depot seal marks the types of cargo that the Ōtaki depot accepts. A rival crate has copied that seal, while a sack of onions carries none. Give the crate the seal it claims and give the sack only its weight. The depot then carries whatever shows the seal, so it takes the rival crate and turns away the sack. Every item reports its weight in grams, and the weight of a load is the sum of those weights.

Read
  • Interface types. Under Basic interfaces, which types belong to an interface's type set when it lists two methods? Under General interfaces, which interfaces can be variable types? Can an interface that lists types be the element type of []Parcel?
  • Uniqueness of identifiers. Read both rules. When does Go treat identically spelled method names as different names?
  • Type assertions. Read the first paragraph. Before checking the stored value, what does x.(T) require of x itself?
Coming from Java

The reflex is sealed interface Parcel permits Letter, Box, and the Java compiler refuses any type absent from that list. Go keeps no such list. A marker method seals nothing while every type sits in one file, as they all do here.

sealed interface Parcel permits Letter, Box {}
record Letter(int grams) implements Parcel {}
Required: sealed
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If carried prints false for the rival's crate, reread the sentence on which types make up a type set. Then list the methods a crate needs to be one of them.
  • If carried prints true for the sack, put the methods on your interface beside the methods you gave the sack.

Goal

A fare barrier calculates the price for each supported ticket type. The Johnsonville barrier knows two ticket types but was built before the day pass existed. It must refuse any ticket that it cannot price and explain why. Tickets reach the barrier either as the ticket itself or as a pointer to it. A Single or a Return earns the same price either way. The refusal keeps ErrUnpriced reachable inside it, so unpriced still finds ErrUnpriced however many more layers a caller adds.

Read
  • Type switches. Find the sentence beginning "Cases then match". What value is compared with each case? Does a pointer match a case that names the pointed-to value's type?
  • errors.Is. Read the paragraph about the error chain. How far does Is search? Does another error with the same message count as a match?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a switch expression over a sealed interface. The Java compiler refuses to build until every permitted type has an arm. Go runs no such check, so a type with no case reaches default and the build still succeeds.

return switch (ticket) {
    case Single s -> 350;
    case Return r -> 620;
};
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If the barrier refuses a ticket you expected it to price, reread what each case is compared against. Then work out the type of a pointer to a Return.
  • If unpriced prints false for an error the barrier made, reread how Is walks the chain. Then find on that same page what puts a new link into it.

testcode.text: n, err := fare(Single{Name: "Ana"}) fmt.Println(n, err == nil) n, err = fare(Return{Name: "Bo"}) fmt.Println(n, err == nil)

expected.text: 0 Tane: no fare for this ticket

testcode.text: n, err := fare(&Return{Name: "Ana"}) fmt.Println(n, err == nil) n, err = fare(&Single{Name: "Bo"}) fmt.Println(n, err == nil)

_, err := fare(DayPass{Name: "Tane"}) fmt.Println(unpriced(err), unpriced(nil)) fmt.Println(unpriced(fmt.Errorf("barrier 3: %w", err)), unpriced(fmt.Errorf("no fare for this ticket"))) _, err = fare(&DayPass{Name: "Mia"}) fmt.Println(err)

expected.text: true false true false Mia: no fare for this ticket
